CDC Statement on Increases in Recent Animal Rabies Activity and Associated Human Exposures Statement For immediate release: September 10, 2026 CDC Media Relations CDC Media Relations (404) 639-3286 media@cdc.gov https://www.cdc.gov/media/ Today, the CDC issued a Health Alert Network (HAN) health advisory to inform clinicians, health departments, and the public about increases in recent animal rabies activity and associated human exposures. Rabies is preventable when people who have been exposed receive appropriate administration of the rabies vaccine before symptoms begin. During the summer of 2026, reports of animal exposures and rabies post-exposure vaccinations have increased across the country. CDC urges clinicians to conduct careful, evidence-based rabies risk assessments and follow current ACIP recommendations when post-exposure vaccination or treatment is indicated. Proper administration of rabies vaccine and human rabies immune globulin is critical to ensuring patients receive effective protection while avoiding unnecessary treatment, costs, and strain on supplies.

Chris Wright Secretary, U.S. Department of Energy Official Photo of Chris Wright, Secretary of the U.S. Department of Energy Chris Wright is the 17 th Secretary for the U.S. Department of Energy. A self-described energy nerd turned entrepreneur, Chris is a dedicated humanitarian with a passion for bringing the benefits of energy to every community in the world. This passion has inspired a career in energy, working not only in oil and gas but nuclear, solar, and geothermal. As Secretary of Energy, Chris is focused on unleashing American energy dominance, accelerating innovation and advancing all energy sources that are affordable, reliable and secure for the American people. Chris completed an undergraduate degree in Mechanical Engineering at MIT and graduate work in Electrical Engineering at UC Berkeley and MIT. He founded Pinnacle Technologies and served as CEO from 1992 to 2006. Pinnacle created the hydraulic fracture mapping industry, and its innovations helped launch commercial shale gas production in the late 1990s. Chris was Chairman of Stroud Energy, an early shale gas producer, before selling to Range Resources in 2006. From anaesthesia and antiseptics, to medical imaging and new, minimally invasive techniques—each innovation has helped surgeons operate with greater confidence and precision. Yet, despite remarkable advances, one challenge has remained: variability. Every patient is different, every procedure is unique, and even the most experienced surgeons must navigate countless decisions before, during, and after the operating room. Nowhere is this variability more evident than in spinal surgery. The human spine is one of the body's most intricate structures, meaning that no two procedures are ever the same. Success depends not only on surgical skill, but on careful planning, execution, and informed decision-making throughout the entire patient journey. From diagnosis to recovery. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us When the Home Front Became the Front Line The Cold War was the defining global influence on the last half of the 20th century. More than merely a military standoff, the Cold War influenced political, economic, cultural, educational, and social programs throughout the United States, the Soviet Union, and other nations. BLM lands in Colorado range from alpine tundra, colorful canyons and mesas in the southwest, to rolling sage covered hills in the northwest. The public owns more than one-third of Colorado. FDA rules have considerable impact on the nation's health, industries, and economy. These rules are not created arbitrarily or in a vacuum, rather they are formed with the public's help.
